title: Being a coequalizer is fpqc local on the target
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: Given morphisms a, b: X to Y and c: Y to Z with c coequalizing a and b after base change to the members of an fpqc covering of Z, and likewise after base change to the pairwise fibre products of that covering, the lemma concludes that c is the coequalizer of a and b (statement lines 4425-4443). The proof explains the mechanism in one step: a morphism from Z to a test scheme is the same thing as a collection of morphisms from the covering members which agree on overlaps, by effectivity of the covering, so the universal property of the coequalizer for Z reduces to the two displayed base change properties (proof lines 4446-4449). The claim is H2: the argument is short, but it identifies precisely which descent property of the covering is being used and why the two hypotheses suffice.
